speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe the timing of your fever—how soon after childbirth it began?  
Doctor: Were there any vaginal bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, or urinary symptoms accompanying the abdominal tenderness?  
Doctor: Do you have any known allergies or recent antibiotic use?  
Doctor: Have you noticed any breast changes or nipple pain?  
Doctor: Can you tell me about the delivery method and any complications during labor?  
Doctor: Any history of previous cesarean sections or uterine surgeries?  
Doctor: Have you experienced any chills, rigors, or fatigue?  
Doctor: Do you have any other abdominal symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea?  
Doctor: Any recent sexual activity or use of intrauterine devices?  
Doctor: What was the last menstrual period prior to pregnancy, and when did you conceive?

speaker: Patient
text: My fever started about 12 hours after delivery, and I haven’t had any vaginal bleeding or foul discharge, but I have been urinating more often. I haven’t taken any antibiotics recently, and I haven’t had any breast issues. The labor was vaginal, but it was prolonged, and I haven’t had a prior cesarean or uterine surgery. I have some fatigue, but no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea, and I haven’t been sexually active since the postpartum period. My last menstrual period was before I got pregnant, and I don’t use intrauterine devices.
